name: 2.0 Turbo Inline-4
notes: Variant: US-market Volkswagen Golf GTI (Mk8, MY2022-2024; VW's specification sheets show the same gearing for the MY2025-2026 facelift) with the EA888 evo4 2.0 TSI (1,984 cc, 82.5 x 92.8 mm, single turbocharger with intercooler; 241 hp SAE, EU 180 kW at 5,000-6,500 rpm) and the optional 7-speed DSG wet dual-clutch gearbox (DQ381 / 0GC family), front-wheel drive, on the standard 18-inch 225/40 R18 92H all-season tyre (S and SE trims; Autobahn: 235/35 R19). Inline-4, one exhaust bank (bank 0): combustion entries are listed in firing order 1-3-4-2 (cylinder 1, 3, 4, 2) at the even 720/4 = 180 deg interval. The firing order is stated in Audi of America's SSP for the third-generation EA888 (2.0 TFSI, same 82.5 x 92.8 mm bore x stroke); VW describes the evo4 as the next-generation EA888 developed from that unit. Gearbox: VW of America's GTI technical specifications give the same two-decimal DSG data for every model year MY2019-2026, printed rounded on the MY2019-2020 and MY2025-2026 sheets (3.40/2.75/1.77/0.93/0.71/0.76/0.64, reverse 2.90, Final I 4.17, Final II 3.13) and truncated on the MY2022-2023 sheets (3.40/2.75/1.76/0.92/0.70/0.75/0.63, Final I 4.16, Final II 3.12; MY2021 and MY2024 mix the two). Together these bracket the true values: the gear ratios are Audi's three-decimal 0GC 7-speed S tronic gear set 3.400/2.750/1.767/0.925/0.705/0.755/0.635 (reverse 2.900; Audi Q2 40 TFSI eTD), Final I lies in [4.165, 4.170) and Final II in [3.125, 3.130); they are modelled as 4.167 and 3.125 (estimate inside the bracket, effect on any ratio < 0.15 %; consistent with a 75-tooth ring gear on 18- and 24-tooth pinions, the same 93/99 tooth sums as Audi's 4.471 = 76/17 and 3.304 = 76/23 0GC pairs - plausibility only). The EPA Test Car List axle field for this car alternates between 3.13 and 3.12 across MY2021-2026, consistent with Final II = 3.125. Per-gear allocation: Audi's technical data for the S3 Cabriolet 7-speed S tronic (August 2017) states 'final drive ratio 1st, 4th, 5th gear 4.471 / 2nd, 3rd, 6th, 7th gear 3.304 / reverse gear 4.471'; that gearbox is the 0GC - VW's 2018 Golf R 7-speed DSG (transmission code 0GC in VW TSB 37-23-01) has the same gear set 3.19/2.75/1.9/1.04/0.79/0.86/0.66 and Final I 4.47 / Final II 3.3 in VW's 2018 Golf R technical specifications, and Audi's Q2 S tronic with the GTI's gear set uses the same 4.471/3.304 pair. So Final I drives 1st, 4th, 5th and reverse, Final II drives 2nd, 3rd, 6th and 7th; this is also the only allocation giving strictly descending overall ratios with an even progression (4th/5th must use Final I and 6th/7th Final II to stay descending; EPA's top-gear axle 3.12/3.13 is Final II). Overall ratios = gear x applicable final drive. EPA N/V screened out: the EPA Test Car Lists give the GTI 7-speed rows axle 3.13/3.12 with N/V 26.7 (MY2022-2023) and 26.6 (MY2024-2026). VW's N/V equals 7th x Final II on the 225/40 R18 tyre's unloaded nominal circumference (1.9844 x 803.9 rev/mile / 60 = 26.6), while the rolling-circumference model (x 0.97) of tests/unit/engines.test.ts gives 27.41 rpm/mph (+3.0 % vs 26.6, +2.7 % vs 26.7), outside the 2.5 % tolerance, so no EPA_NV row is used (a manufacturer N/V convention, not a ratio conflict). Estimated (not published in the sources used): redline 6,500 rpm = the end of VW's rated-power band (no maximum engine speed is published in the sources used); limiter type ignition-soft at 6,600 rpm with 150 rpm hysteresis; idle 700 rpm; shift time 0.10 s (DCT type default; VW states no shift time). Source differences are rounding only (gearbox, above) and the torque-band end by market/year (EU 1,600-4,300 rpm, US MY2025-2026 1,600-4,500 rpm), which does not enter the data.
